transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-20
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Ramirez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Maya Gupta (Lyra Head of MLOps), Daniel Park (Lyra VP Eng), Priya Nair (Lyra Security Architect)

00:00 - 00:15 Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off, this is Sofia from Redwood, i have Ethan our SE with me. quick round - can you introduce yourselves?
00:15 - 00:30 Maya: Maya here, head of MLOps at Lyra, we run most models in our private clusters, lots of PHI so on prem is a must. Daniel's here too.
00:30 - 00:45 Daniel: Hey all. we are evaluating options: hosted is out due to data residency and regs, looking at dedicated vs private on-prem, and specifically air-gapped.
00:45 - 01:00 Ethan: great, thanks. quick agenda: understand constraints, talk about Redwood Private on-prem flow, offline update story, hardware/benchmark needs, and pilot next steps. does that sound right?
01:00 - 01:15 Maya: yes, and we need to validate the signed delivery process for models and how key rotation works without outbound internet.

01:30 - 02:00 Ethan: high level on Redwood Private: we provide a control plane that can be run in your VPC or an appliance for fully air-gapped installs. for air-gapped specifically, we ship a signed bundle (models, runtime, containers) that you can import via secure media. the control plane can be configured to run entirely disconnected; updates are applied via signed packages.
02:00 - 02:25 Priya: okay signed bundles sound good, but what about key management - do you require external KMS calls? how do we do key rotation?
02:25 - 02:50 Ethan: we support customer-managed KMS; for air-gapped we support HSM integrations and bring-your-own-keys. we also have an offline key-rotation tool that generates rotation manifests which you sign with your HSM and then apply locally. it's a bit of a manual flow for fully disconnected environments but it's supported.
02:50 - 03:10 Priya: hmm, manual flows are fine but we need auditability - every rotation must be logged and verifiable for audits.
03:10 - 03:40 Sofia: yes, we export audit logs and a tamper-evident chain of custody for model updates. we'll include our audit log schema in the security pack.

04:00 - 04:30 Daniel: hardware question - our infra team uses Dell R750xa nodes, mostly A100-class GPUs, sometimes older V100 in DR racks. memory for models is constrained, we also have limited NVMe on some nodes.
04:30 - 05:00 Ethan: okay that matters. model selection and quantization profiles can reduce RAM and GPU memory. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization/FP16 or int8 profiles, and the runtime can run quantized models but some ops are slower. we'll need to benchmark your typical prompts.
05:00 - 05:20 Maya: do you support 4-bit quantization and does the KV cache and streaming work with quantized weights?
05:20 - 05:40 Ethan: yes we have 4-bit q support for many open models; KV cache is preserved but some kernel paths differ so throughput changes. streaming is supported but you'll see per-token latency differences; we'll capture that in the benchmark.

06:00 - 06:40 Priya: networking: can we keep all inference traffic inside the enclave? no egress allowed. how do updates get validated without internet?
06:40 - 07:00 Ethan: updates come as signed tarballs. we provide a verification tool that validates signatures and checksums; that tool is standalone so it can run in the air-gapped environment. package signatures are rooted in Redwood's signing key but can also be validated against a customer-controlled root cert if you prefer.
07:00 - 07:20 Priya: can we require dual signatures (Redwood + Lyra) for model updates?
07:20 - 07:50 Sofia: yes we can support customizable signing policies — we'll propose an approach: Redwood signs release, you re-sign with your HSM before import. we'll detail that in the security doc.

08:00 - 09:00 Daniel: what about vulnerability patching and CVE management? if you're air-gapped, how fast can we get security patches?
09:00 - 09:20 Ethan: we maintain an offline patch bundle on a cadence; for critical CVEs we push an emergency signed patch. turn-around depends on severity but we have SLA options on Dedicated/Private for expedited patches.
09:20 - 09:40 Maya: and software dependencies? our security team insists on a SBOM for all components.
09:40 - 10:00 Sofia: we produce SBOMs and will include them in the security pack; for on-prem installs we also provide a reproducible build hash and provenance for each container.

10:30 - 11:00 Maya: about model ops — we need the ability to run A/B rollouts and canary on a subset of hosts without internet. can Redwood handle internal routing policies?
11:00 - 11:30 Ethan: yes the runtime supports per-host routing and canary labels; you can pin tenants or routes to specific model versions and do manual or time-based rollouts. the control plane UI is optional in air-gapped mode — ops can run the CLI to trigger rollouts. logs and metrics are shipped to your internal TSDB.

12:00 - 13:00 Daniel: cost/throughput — we care about latency SLOs for real-time triage flows (sub-200ms ideally for short prompts) but also cost for batch tasks. what's a realistic expectation on our A100 rigs?
13:00 - 13:25 Ethan: for short prompts on A100-80GB you can get sub-200ms for smaller models (e.g., Llama-2-13B quantized) with appropriate batching config and low prefix lengths; larger models will be higher. caching and prefix reuse help a lot. we'll simulate your prompt distribution in the benchmark.
13:25 - 13:50 Maya: do you support KV caching across restarts or is it ephemeral in-memory?
13:50 - 14:10 Ethan: KV cache is in-memory by default; for warm-starting we have a checkpointing mechanism to persist popular KV entries to NVMe, but that requires NVMe on the node. we'll note which nodes need local NVMe in our hardware checklist.

15:00 - 15:30 Priya: legal/contract — we need clear indemnities around PHI, plus proof that models won't leak training data. any standard clauses?
15:30 - 16:00 Sofia: we have enterprise legal templates for Private deployments and can add PHI-specific language. on the model leakage side, we recommend red-team evals; Redwood offers eval tooling for privacy/regression checks as an add-on. we'll route this to Legal.

16:30 - 17:00 Maya: pilot scope — we'd like a 3-month pilot: 2 nodes initially, run our triage/clinical prompts, validate latency/throughput, evaluate offline update flow and audits.
17:00 - 17:30 Ethan: that's doable. pilot artifacts: we'll provide the signed runtime and model bundles, benchmark harness, and a limited support SLA for the pilot.

18:00 - 19:00 Sofia: recap: Sofia will send security pack (SOC2, ISO docs, SBOMs, audit log schema), Ethan will prepare benchmark script and on-prem install checklist, Maya will share hardware inventory and network diagram, Priya will confirm signing and key rotation constraints. we'll aim to run benchmarks next week.

19:30 - 20:00 Daniel: fine; also, can you share a sample of the offline package verification tool and example logs?
20:00 - 20:30 Sofia: yes, we'll include a small example in the security pack and a link to the install guide.

21:00 - 21:30 Maya: thanks all, this was useful. we'll regroup after the hardware doc.
21:30 - 21:45 Sofia: thanks, everyone.

Notes/Artifacts referenced: Security pack link (placeholder): https://redwood.ai/security-pack/lyra-sample (will be shared), Install guide: redwood-onprem-install-v2.pdf (shared on follow-up), Benchmark harness: redwood-bench-runner v0.9

Transcript quirks: occasional mis-heard words, speaker labels sometimes shifted in auto-transcript, proper nouns like "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes transcribed as "Redwood Dedicted" or "Redwood Privatee".
questions: How are model updates validated in air-gapped environments?
Can Redwood integrate with our HSM for key rotation?
What quantization profiles do you recommend for A100 vs V100?
How are audit logs exported and are they tamper-evident?
